1. Introduction

This manual provides comprehensive operational guidance for the Atlas platform. It covers standard operating procedures, safety protocols, and maintenance routines necessary for reliable service delivery.

Personnel assigned to Atlas duties must study this manual thoroughly and demonstrate competency before unsupervised operation. Updates are distributed via the internal change management system.

Scope
Applies to all hardware and software components within the Atlas ecosystem.

2. Scope

The scope of this manual includes all operational, maintenance, and administrative activities related to the Atlas platform. Exclusions are noted in the appendix.

Scope changes require a formal revision request approved by the configuration control board.

In scope
Core services, support infrastructure, monitoring, and incident response.
Out of scope
Third-party integrations not certified by Atlas governance.
Boundary
Physical data centers and cloud tenancies designated as production.
Assumptionspsis
Personnel hold valid certifications and have access to required tools.

Definitions are maintained by the technical writing team and updated upon approval of a change request.

4. Safety

All personnel must follow established safety protocols when operating Atlas hardware. Failure to comply may result in equipment damage or personal injury.

Emergency procedures are posted in each data center and included in the onboarding checklist.

PPE
Personal protective equipment required in server rooms.
LOTO
Lockout/tagout procedures for maintenance.
ESD

5. Procedures

Standard operating procedures (SOPs) ensure consistent execution of routine and emergency tasks. Each procedure includes prerequisites, steps, verification, and rollback instructions.

Procedures are versioned and require sign-off from the responsible engineering lead before deployment.

SOP
Standard operating procedure document.
Prerequisite
Condition that must be true before starting.
Rollback
Steps to revert to a prior known-good state.
Verification
Confirmation that the procedure succeeded.

6. Maintenance

Preventive and corrective maintenance activities are scheduled to minimize downtime and extend equipment lifespan. All maintenance windows must be approved through the change advisory board.

Technicians must record work performed in the maintenance log and verify system health before closing the window.

Preventive
Scheduled tasks to prevent failure.
Corrective
Unplanned tasks to fix existing failures.
Predictive
Data-driven tasks based on condition monitoring.
Window
Approved time slot for maintenance.
